answer: Men and women have generally remained in assigned roles for most of history, and according to modern neuroscience, the male brain is wired for provider work while the female brain is predisposed to caregiving responsibilities. Therefore, it is natural and efficient for men to focus mainly on high-risk jobs outside the home and for women to spend most of their time addressing domestic and family duties. While equality in debate is an ideal, in practice separate roles serve both sexes well and align with their respective biological strengths, minimizing the potential for conflict or inefficiency and preserving traditional family structures.
